findings.text: H2342J and H2342K (chul, 9 verses combined, glossed to twist: dance and to twist: anticipate) have no bearing on moral perversion: every verse is literal, a woman dancing (2 Sam 3:29's negated wish), waiting anxiously (Ps 37:7, Mic 1:12, Judg 3:25), a dove sent out and waited for (Gen 8:10). The root's full range (dance, whirl, writhe in labor, wait) has nothing to do with corruption; it was pulled into this family only because one of its senses translates as twist. The two codes are gloss-homonym noise, not a shared concept.

findings.text: H7806 (shazar, 19 verses, the family's single largest strong) is glossed to twist, but every one of its 19 citations is literal tabernacle-construction material, fine twined linen repeated almost verbatim through Exodus 26 to 39 (curtains, the ephod, the breastpiece, the veil). It is technical textile vocabulary, not moral language at all; with the chul codes it accounts for 28 of the family's about 98 verses, a gloss-text-grouping failure of the same kind as family R and G0073.

findings.text: H5753A/B (avah) makes the metaphor's two halves visible in one root split into two codes: the physical sense (bent, bowed down in pain and anguish, Isa 21:3, Ps 38:6) and the moral sense (the confession formula we have sinned and acted perversely, 1 Kgs 8:47, 2 Chr 6:37, Dan 9:5) are literally the same Hebrew word, split only for cataloguing.

The justice and judiciary sub-theme recurs strongly: H5557 (salaph) and H5791 (avat) are both explicitly about bribery and perverting legal judgment (a bribe subverts the cause of the righteous, Exod 23:8, Deut 16:19; does God pervert justice, Job 8:3, 34:12), and H6127 and H6140 apply the same crooked language to justice itself (justice goes forth perverted, Hab 1:4; make crooked all that is straight, Mic 3:9). This is the third family, after D and G, to converge independently on judicial and legal-fairness vocabulary: corruption of justice specifically, not wrongdoing in general.

G1294 (diastrephō) carries the identical figure into Greek, applied collectively: faithless and twisted generation (Matt 17:17, Luke 9:41), crooked and twisted generation (Phil 2:15). Moral deviation as physical distortion is applied to a whole people, not just an individual, and its own LSJ entry confirms the base sense is genuinely physical (distorted eyes, limbs, warped wood) before any moral extension.

Prov 10:9 and 28:18 (walks in integrity, crooked in his ways) and Eccl 1:15 (what is crooked cannot be made straight) state the straight and crooked = righteous and wicked mapping almost as a proverb-form axiom, the most direct statement of the crooked-body metaphor found in this exercise.
